subject: Jonah Patel — score variance triage and next step
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Jonah Patel — quick debrief + scoring gap

Team — quick one. Jonah interviewed yesterday (System Design + Platform deep dive). I pulled the scorecards in GH and there's a clear variance on the System Design section: Marissa gave a 4/5, Aditya a 2/5. We need a short rationale from each interviewer so we can decide next steps (onsite/skip or manager consult).

Ask: please reply with a one-sentence rationale for your System Design score and note any red flags we should surface to Hiring Manager. If possible, attach the scorecard export. I'll collate and propose next step by 2pm PT.

Key context (brief):
- Role: Senior Platform Engineer (staff hire loop)
- Focus area for this loop: distributed state, cache invalidation, multi-tenant failures
- Candidate has strong product sense and ownership examples; the divergence is technical depth/application to scale.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Staff PM, Talent Liaison — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Jonah Patel — quick debrief + scoring gap

Jordan — attaching my completed scorecard (jonah_patel_scorecard_marissa.pdf). Short rationale on System Design: I scored a 4 because Jonah articulated a clear partitioning strategy for multi-tenant state and proposed a pragmatic cache invalidation TTL/hint system that balanced correctness and operational cost. He sketched failure modes and suggested safe degradation paths (read-through fallback + per-tenant circuit breaker). No major red flags — primary weakness was limited discussion of cross-datacenter replication tradeoffs (time was limited).

Bullet notes:
- Strengths: clear tradeoff reasoning, good ops runbook instincts
- Concern: didn't quantifiably reason about cross-region consensus/latency limits (would like to see more specifics if we progress)

—Marissa
Senior SWE, Distributed Systems

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Jonah Patel — quick debrief + scoring gap

On Thu, Mar 25, 2027 at 10:01 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan — attaching my completed scorecard (jonah_patel_scorecard_marissa.pdf). Short rationale on System Design: I scored a 4 because Jonah articulated a clear partitioning strategy...

Thanks for the notes. I uploaded my scorecard (jonah_patel_scorecard_aditya.pdf). Short rationale: I landed at 2 because while Jonah covered a reasonable high-level approach, when pressed on cache eviction correctness under concurrent tenant state updates he deferred to "we'd build a test harness" instead of sketching a concrete algorithm or showing an understanding of eventual consistency guarantees at scale. That gap matters for this role — we need people who can either propose a lock-free approach or clearly show why eventual consistency is acceptable and how we'd verify it.

Quick proposal: If we can't reach a 3/above consensus, can we run a 20-minute follow-up technical sync between Jonah and a systems SME (I can do it) to focus specifically on correctness under concurrent updates? That will cost a little time but avoid false negatives.

- Aditya
Principal SWE, Storage & Runtime

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Jonah Patel — quick debrief + scoring gap

I saw both cards — agree there's a substantive difference but not an automatic reject. My read: candidate shows engineering judgment and would likely get to a solid design with a short follow-up around the concurrent update correctness question. I'm okay with Aditya running a focused 20-min follow-up; if Jonah can demonstrate a concrete approach, move to hiring manager consult.

Also added candidate record to GH: candidate_record_GH-12345.pdf for your reference.

Mina
Engineering Manager, Platform Reliability

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Jonah Patel — quick debrief + scoring gap

Thanks all — appreciate the quick replies and the uploads. Plan: Aditya, please run the 20-minute follow-up (you, Jonah, + 5-min me intro) — try to schedule for tomorrow morning PT if Jonah's available. Mina and Marissa: if Aditya's convinced after the follow-up, we'll loop in Hiring Manager (Lydia) for a 30-min consult; otherwise we'll decide not to advance.

Action items: 
- Aditya: send candidate a calendar invite (20 min + buffer) and copy me — aim for 2027-03-26 morning PT.
- Marissa: if you want, consolidate a one-paragraph summary after the follow-up (use the GH candidate doc link above).
- Mina: I'll prep the Hiring Manager brief if we move forward.

I'll update the GH record and ping Talent Ops after the follow-up.

Jordan
